domain: sovereign lending / loan-lifecycle execution outcome prediction (World Bank Group)
prediction_question: At the instant the World Bank Board approves an IBRD loan (board_approval_date, a documented column: 'The date the World Bank approves the loan'), will that loan disburse at least 90% of its original principal amount over its life? (Alternative near-balanced threshold >=99% is measured and recorded; construction picks one and documents it.) A useful prediction enables disbursement-risk scoring at commitment time for portfolio management, borrower-side planning and development-finance research: roughly a third of IBRD lending historically fails to move 90% of its commitment, and that gap is the operational quantity WB cash planning and aid-delivery studies care about.
prediction_time: The instant is the Board Approval Date, published by the World Bank at approval time (the same-day press release and projects.worldbank.org record carry it; the dataset column is documented as 'The date the World Bank approves the loan'). Features are the approval-time attributes documented by the publisher: country/economy + code, borrower, guarantor, loan_type, original_principal_amount, currency_of_commitment, project_id/project_name, board approval fiscal/calendar year. CAVEAT (documented by the publisher itself): the `region` column description reads 'Country/Economy lending is grouped into regions based on the current World Bank administrative (rather than geographic) region' - i.e. current-vintage coding, so for pre-2011 approvals region may be back-coded; the shipped task must either drop `region` or carry this as a disclosed current-vintage limitation (both options stated; construction decides, qualification enforces). All other shipped features are static attributes fixed at approval. The label resolves later, at the end of the loan's disbursement window (closed_date_most_recent / terminal loan_status), so the whole target window follows the prediction instant. Censoring is measured: approvals through 2017 are >=94% disbursement-closed by the 2026-09-30 snapshot (2010-2017: 0-6 open per approval year), so the labeled population is censored at 2017 approvals and this cutoff is recorded in the shipped rows.
target_definition: Binary completion label: final_disbursed_ratio = disbursed_amount / original_principal_amount >= 0.90 (primary) or >= 0.99 (near-balanced alternative, base rate 51.5%), computed only on instruments whose disbursement phase is closed (terminal loan_status - Fully Repaid/Cancelled/Disbursed/Transferred, Terminated - or Repaying, or closed_date <= data-as-of; 'Repaying' with undisbursed>0 occurs on 2/9538 rows and is excluded by construction). Label source columns (disbursed_amount, undisbursed_amount, cancelled_amount, closed_date_most_recent, last_disbursement_date, loan_status, all repayment fields) are excluded from shipped features. Zero ratio (312 IBRD rows, fully cancelled/terminated with cancelled_amount = original) is a genuine negative (no disbursement ever made), distinguished from missing data by the in-row cancelled_amount. Population: IBRD instruments from DS00047 with original_principal_amount > 0, excluding guarantees (loan_number prefixes IBRDB/IBRDG, 113 rows) and B-loan/guarantee-facility types (BLNR 18, BLNC 2, GURB 84, GUBF 9); the type mix is recorded so construction can scope further with evidence.

split_strategy: Temporal splits on board_approval calendar year, labeled population censored at 2017 approvals (measured: >=94% of 2010-2017 approvals are disbursement-closed in the 2026-09-30 snapshot, 0-6 open rows per year; 2018+ approvals are 12-96% still open and are excluded as censored, per-year counts recorded in measurements). review: All five discovery contracts have measured evidence. (1) Redistribution: CC BY 4.0 stated on the dataset page and metadata API - class A. (2) Prediction timing: instant is the documented board_approval_date; all shipped features are static approval-time attributes, with one disclosed current-vintage caveat (region, flagged in the publisher's own column description) that construction must either drop or carry as a limitation; the whole label window follows the instant; censoring is measured and the population cutoff at 2017 approvals is explicit. (3) Target: ratio of two in-row columns, label sources excludable, zero-ratio instruments are genuine negatives (cancelled_amount documents them), not missing data. (4) Split capacity: both classes in all three windows with hundreds of independent country-year clusters; clustering by project_id and country-year is measured and the split rule accounts for it. (5) Not a mirror: no ML-ready disbursement-completion benchmark exists; prior art targets IEG ratings (different target, different table, already measured as no-headroom by our own dropped wb-ieg candidate). Headroom is the known open risk of this source family (the IEG task failed it) - that is a construction/qualification measurement, and the near-balanced >=99% variant plus the approval-time-only feature contract are the mitigations; the honest posture is to build and let the measured baselines decide, not to claim headroom now.
verdict: No demonstrated headroom under this protocol. The harness runner's own baseline reached eval AUC 0.5452 on the accepted artifact (train.py and validate.py agree exactly), against a train-estimated country identity prior of 0.5364, an instrument-type prior of 0.5156 and a country-persistence reference of 0.4771 on the same 1,034 eval rows. The observed gap over the country prior is +0.0088; the marginal standard errors are about 0.019 each, so the difference is far inside sampling noise - an inconclusive difference, not parity and not a demonstrated edge. Nothing here proves the question is unanswerable; it says this source's approval-instant fields do not carry it.
next_action: None (dropped 2026-10-29). Negative finding preserved in measurements.baseline_2026_10_29 and in staging release 427393678. Reopen only as a NEW task instance with approval-instant information the source table does not carry (e.g. a verified as-of country/macro covariate join with its own availability ledger), or a change target; do not re-tune this label, threshold or these splits.
construction_script: candidates/wb-loan-disbursement-completion/source/build.py (worker job wb-sol-002 in flight; construct-only, no performance metric computed anywhere in the build; gate + --accept + score.py references run in the fixed run.sh order)
rejection_reason: Measured no headroom over an identity prior at the Board-approval instant. Diagnosis, bounded: the shipped features at the instant are the instrument's static attributes (loan_type, original_principal_amount, borrower/guarantor identity, country) plus identifiers; the label is highly persistent (68-69% positive in every split) and country identity carries nearly all of the observable signal. There is no within-row history and no macro/country-year covariate in DS00047 at the approval instant, so the tested model has little beyond the prior to learn from. The negative finding is preserved: artifact c9ac51b846f7b1ee, gate 1.5.0 report cad5d763, worker job wb-sol-baseline-001 (staging release 427393678). Holdout was never scored (no holdout evaluation ran), so the sealed split remains unused.
